decisions.rationale: Full name of a single defined disease (late-onset familial Mediterranean fever); the whole phrase is kept as the most specific minimal span.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease) and 5 (minimum necessary span)

decisions.rationale: Abbreviation FMF in parentheses after the long form names the same specific disease and is annotated as a separate synonymous mention.
Long form of the specific disease familial Mediterranean fever in the abstract.
Abbreviation FMF defined in parentheses after the long form; annotated as its own mention.
FMF is used as a modifier of the noun attack (first FMF attack) rather than naming a disease as a stand-alone noun phrase.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (Modifiers for other concepts)

decisions.rationale: FMF modifies the noun clinic (FMF clinic), so it is a disease name used as a modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (Modifiers for other concepts)

decisions.rationale: FMF modifies the noun patients (FMF patients), so it is used as a modifier of another concept.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (Modifiers for other concepts)

decisions.rationale: FMF modifies the noun clinic (FMF clinic) and is used as a modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (Modifiers for other concepts)

decisions.rationale: The word disease is a very general term used for the condition in general and is excluded.
FMF modifies the noun gene (FMF gene), so it is a disease name used as a modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (Modifiers for other concepts)

decisions.rationale: Late-onset FMF denotes a particular, defined form of the specific disease FMF, similar to classical galactosemia, and is annotated as one specific disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease) and Examples 15 (form of disease)

decisions.rationale: The word disease is a very general term (their disease) and is excluded.
FMF is the head of the phrase manifestations of FMF and refers to the disease itself, not a modifier of another noun.
Amyloidosis is a family of multiple specific diseases (for example AL and AA amyloidosis), so it is a disease class.
Chronic arthritis is a grouping of several specific arthritic diseases and is therefore described as a family of diseases.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Disease Class) and Examples 11 (grey-area terms)

decisions.rationale: Myalgia names a single defined muscular condition that can be linked to one definition, so it is annotated as a specific disease rather than as a general term.
The word disease is a very general term describing severity and is excluded.
FMF modifies the noun population (FMF population), so it is used as a modifier of another concept.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (Modifiers for other concepts)

decisions.rationale: FMF is the complement of the noun onset (onset of FMF) and names the specific disease itself rather than modifying another noun.
The word disease is a very general term (a milder form of disease) and is excluded.
